# Appeal of Prior Authorization Denial — Request for Reconsideration

**RE:** Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated August 25, 2026
**Member:** Jordan Kimura
**Member ID:** W450262274
**Reference number:** POC-9297E0E467-45895
**Service denied:** Bunion surgery (hallux valgus), CPT 28296
**Plan:** MedStar Family Choice (Commercial/ACA), Maryland
**Governing policy:** *Utilization Management (UM) Criteria*, effective July 2026 — https://www.medstarfamilychoicemd.com/-/media/project/mho/mfc/maryland-healthchoice-physicians/medical-policies-and-procedures/policy-115-utilization-management-um-criteria-july-2026.pdf

**Date:** [Date you are sending this letter]

**To:** MedStar Family Choice — Member Appeals
[Use the appeal address printed on my denial letter, or the address given by the number on the back of my insurance card]

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization request for bunion surgery (hallux valgus correction), CPT 28296, which MedStar Family Choice denied on August 25, 2026. The notice states that the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision and approve the surgery. My surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, MD, orthopedic surgery, has documented that this procedure is needed.

## The plan's own policy, and what my records show

The plan's *Utilization Management (UM) Criteria* policy states:

> "MedStar Family Choice follows documented UM criteria to facilitate consistency in UM decision making."

and

> "MFC pre-authorization decisions are based on the following criteria:"

That sentence ends in a colon and introduces a list of criteria that was not included in the material I was given, and I have not been told which of those criteria was applied to my request or what imaging finding it requires. I want to be straightforward with you about this: **I am not quoting any imaging threshold as the plan's requirement, because no such threshold appears in the policy language available to me.** The plan holds that language. I am therefore arguing from the facts in my chart, and asking the plan to identify the specific criterion it used.

Here is what the records submitted with my request document:

- **Imaging.** Weight-bearing foot radiographs taken July 26, 2026 show a hallux valgus angle of 38 degrees and an intermetatarsal angle of 17 degrees. These are objective, measured findings from weight-bearing films — the imaging the plan says does not support the request is in fact a measured radiographic deformity.
- **Duration and course.** I have had 18 months of progressive pain in the foot, unrelieved by rest.
- **Conservative treatment, completed.** Activity modification, wide toe-box footwear and a custom orthotic over 8 weeks, from May 19, 2026 to July 14, 2026, with 20 visits completed, documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- **Medication trials.** NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief, and a corticosteroid injection on May 7, 2026 that gave only 4 weeks of partial relief.
- **Examination.** Positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain.
- **Function and risk.** I cannot tolerate closed shoes, and there is ulceration risk over the prominence.
- **Surgical candidacy.** No active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, non-smoker.

The policy also states:

> "Upon review for medical necessity, requests for ongoing services or treatment that have not demonstrated improvement in condition or benefit to the member will be subject to denial as not medically necessary."

My record is the mirror image of that standard. The non-surgical care I completed — bracing and orthotic therapy, footwear change, activity modification, months of NSAIDs, and an injection — is exactly the treatment that did not produce lasting improvement or benefit. The injection helped for four weeks. The pain has been progressive across 18 months. Continuing the same conservative measures is the course that has already failed; surgery is the next step my surgeon has documented as necessary.

## Request for the criteria the plan actually applied

I am asking, in writing, for the specific rule or criterion relied upon in denying my request. The plan's own policy says:

> "All criteria utilized in utilization management are available upon request."

and

> "To request specific utilization management criteria or to speak with a Medical Director, please contact us by phone during our normal business hours, 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM Monday through Friday, at 800-905-1722 or 410-933-2200 option 2, then option 1."

I am making that request here, as the member, and I am asking for it in writing at no cost to me. If the review used a licensed or proprietary criteria set rather than a publicly posted document, I am asking for the name of that criteria set, the specific subset and edition used, and the full text of the criteria applied to my determination. If the imaging findings in my chart fall short of a specific measured threshold, I am asking the plan to state that threshold, identify the source, and explain how my radiographic measurements of a 38-degree hallux valgus angle and a 17-degree intermetatarsal angle were compared against it. I cannot meaningfully respond to an imaging-based denial without knowing the imaging standard that was used.

## What I am asking for

I ask that MedStar Family Choice overturn the August 25, 2026 denial and authorize bunion surgery (hallux valgus correction), CPT 28296, as requested by Dr. Marchetti. I also ask that this appeal be reviewed by a clinician with relevant expertise, and that I receive the criteria requested above and a written explanation of the decision.

I understand my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice, by **February 21, 2027**, and I am submitting it within that period. I am sending it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter; if the correct filing location differs, please forward this appeal to the proper department and let me know.

Please contact me if any further records would help. My surgeon's office can also provide additional documentation on request.

Thank you for reviewing this carefully.

Sincerely,

**Jordan Kimura**
Member ID: W450262274
[Street address]
[City, State ZIP]
[Phone number]
[Email address]

**Enclosures:**
- Copy of denial notice dated August 25, 2026 (Reference POC-9297E0E467-45895)
- Weight-bearing foot radiograph report, July 26, 2026
- Physical therapy discharge note (May 19, 2026 – July 14, 2026, 20 visits)
- Office notes and surgical recommendation from Dr. Marchetti, MD
- Injection and medication records
- [Any other records you wish to attach]

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
